app.initial_help:
👆 Enter a ticker, pick a model, and click **🔍 Analyze**.

**Examples:** `AAPL` · `TSLA` · `MSFT` · `RELIANCE.NS` · `TCS.NS`

Every model is benchmarked against a naive 'tomorrow = today' baseline — if it can't beat that, the app will tell you.
app.backtest_header: 🧪 Walk-Forward Backtest — Model vs. Naive Baseline
app.backtest_caption: {model_name} vs. a 'tomorrow's close = today's close' baseline, averaged across {n_folds} expanding-window, chronological folds.
app.directional_accuracy_caption: Directional accuracy is judged against a 50% coin flip, not the naive baseline — the baseline always predicts 'no change,' which has no direction to be right or wrong about, so it isn't a meaningful comparison for this particular metric. It's still the right comparison for price error (above), where 'no change' is a real prediction with a real error to measure.
app.beats_neither_warning: ⚠️ **{model_name} beat neither a coin flip on direction nor the naive baseline on price error** for this ticker/window. That's a real, useful result — it means there's no exploitable signal in these features for this stock right now, not that the app is broken. Try a different model or ticker.
app.held_out_fold_header: 🔬 Most Recent Held-Out Fold: Actual vs Predicted
app.prediction_caption_with_interval: Model: {model_name} · predicted log-return: {log_return} · last close: ${last_close} · {confidence} interval: ${low} – ${high} (from real walk-forward backtest error, not a guess)
app.track_record_pointer: This prediction has been recorded and will be checked against the real close once {date} has passed — see the **Track Record** page for how {model_name} has actually done on {ticker} (and other tickers) over time.
app.drift_warning: ⚠️ **Feature drift detected** in {n_drifted} of {n_total} feature(s) — the last {current_window} trading days look statistically different from the {reference_window} days before them ({feature_list}). Backtest metrics above were computed over the full history and may not reflect current conditions as reliably.
app.news_sentiment_caption: Descriptive context only — recent headlines, not fed into the model. Free news sources don't provide a historical archive, so there's no honest way to have backtested this.
app.no_headlines: No recent headlines found for this ticker.
watchlist.title: 📈 Watchlist Comparison
watchlist.caption: Runs the same walk-forward-backtested prediction across several tickers at once, so you can see which ones actually show a model edge over the naive baseline instead of checking one at a time.
watchlist.initial_help: Enter a few tickers and click **🔍 Compare**.
watchlist.color_caption: Color marks direction (green = predicted gain, red = predicted loss) and every bar is also labeled with its value — color is never the only signal.
track_record.title: 📊 Track Record
track_record.caption: Every prediction you make anywhere in this app is recorded before its outcome is known, then checked against the real close once its target date has passed. This page is your receipts — not a claim, a record. (Only your own predictions — everyone's track record here is their own.)
track_record.no_records_info: No predictions recorded yet. Analyze a ticker on the **app** or **watchlist** page, and it'll show up here once its target date has passed.
track_record.scatter_caption: Each point is one resolved prediction. The x-axis is what the model predicted would change; the y-axis is what actually happened. Points on the diagonal line were spot-on; points in the top-right or bottom-left quadrants at least called the right direction, even if the size was off.
track_record.no_resolved_info: No resolved predictions yet for this filter — check back after their target dates pass.
monitoring.title: 🩺 Model Monitoring
monitoring.caption: One entry per ticker/model/day — every backtest run updates that day's row rather than piling up duplicates, so this reflects how each model has actually looked over time, not how many times someone clicked Analyze. (Scoped to your own analyses — not a dashboard shared across everyone using this app.)
monitoring.admin_caption: System-wide model health across every user of this app — one entry per user/ticker/model/day. Admin-only (see the Authentication section of the README).
monitoring.no_backtests_info: No backtests logged yet. Analyze a ticker on the **app** or **watchlist** page and it'll show up here.
monitoring.no_runs_info: No logged runs for this ticker/model combination yet.
monitoring.accuracy_chart_caption: Per model, against the 50% coin-flip floor (dashed) — not the naive baseline, for the same reason the main app doesn't compare them directly there.
monitoring.rmse_chart_caption: Model vs. the naive baseline, in the same dollar units — lower is better for both.
monitoring.drift_warning: ⚠️ Feature drift was detected on {drift_days} of {logged_days} logged day(s) for {ticker}. Backtest metrics from drifted days may not reflect current market behavior as reliably — see the per-day breakdown below.
prediction.title: 📈 Stock Price Prediction
prediction.no_data_warning: ⚠️ No historical data for **{ticker}**. Try a different exchange (BSE ↔ NSE) or period.
prediction.forecast_caption: AutoReg model trained on 2 years of daily close prices (90% train / 10% test). Forecasts beyond a few days compound their own error at every step — treat the far end of the dotted line as illustrative, not a real price target.
prediction.forecast_failed_warning:
⚠️ Could not generate a forecast for **{ticker}**.

This usually means Yahoo Finance returned insufficient history for this symbol. Try switching the exchange (BSE ↔ NSE) or selecting a different stock.
